question: Two years after a water outbreak, 36% of infected townspeople had irritable bowel syndrome, as did 10% of the uninfected. Extra cases per 1,000 infected?
move: Subtract what would have happened anyway before crediting a cause.
trap: Blaming the infection for all 360 cases, ignoring the background rate.
hint: Some infected people would have developed the condition without any outbreak.
steps: Cases expected anyway, at the uninfected rate: 10% of 1,000 = 100.
reference: Marshall, Thabane, Garg et al., Incidence and epidemiology of irritable bowel syndrome after a large waterborne outbreak of bacterial dysentery, Gastroenterology, 2006
